title: Departments paid mostly through other departments’ budgets
question: Which departments recover the largest share of their costs from other departments, and where did those recoveries grow fastest?
finding: 5 departments recovered half or more of their day-to-day spending from other departments in fiscal 2026: Technology (89%, $157.0 million); Human Resources (85%, $128.7 million); Controller (77%, $68.4 million); City Attorney (71%, $94.3 million); City Administrator (63%, $325.3 million). Their cost appears in the budgets of the departments they bill, not as a budget line of their own, which is what an internal charge is for and also what makes it hard to see in a budget hearing. Recoveries at least doubled since fiscal 2019 at Emergency Management ($2.2 million to $15.8 million); Treasurer-Tax Collector ($4.2 million to $16.4 million); Homelessness Services ($5.5 million to $19.7 million); Fire Department ($5.9 million to $17.0 million).
how: For each department: revenue lines of the kind “Expenditure Recovery” in fiscal 2019 and fiscal 2026, set against the department’s own day-to-day spending. The largest payer is the sub-account that brought in the most in fiscal 2026, under the ledger’s own label (it names the department billed). Departments recovering under $5 million in fiscal 2026 are left out. Sorted by share.
limits: Central services are meant to be paid this way, and a high share is the design working: technology, human resources, the City Attorney, the Controller and the City Administrator exist largely to serve other departments. The share can pass 100% where a department bills for costs it books elsewhere. The files show who paid and how much; they do not show hours, unit prices or whether the buyer could refuse. The audit of April 2025 found that the cost models behind centrally budgeted charges are documented in formats that vary widely, which it says complicates the budget office’s review. What would settle whether a recovery is priced fairly: the cost model each billing department gives the budget office.
